audit.title: Multiple-Variable Response (MVR) Feeds

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Strong; opens with "MVR feeds bundle multiple data points into a single onchain update," a self-contained definition. No action needed beyond section leads (see below).

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong; 4 clean sections, median 80 words, one table, 0 level skips. Ideal chunk sizes for RAG.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Weak; 8 numerals, 0 with units, vague quantifiers "various"/"most". No stated field limits, decimals behavior, gas/efficiency numbers, or bytes-decoding specifics.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Adequate internal linking (11 links) but 0 external/primary sources; nothing links to a spec or canonical concept anchor for context.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Good; both "MVR feeds" and `BundleAggregatorProxy` are defined crisply near first use.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak; measured facts show 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, datePublished/dateModified absent. No freshness signal for engines to trust.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: Weak; 0 fenced blocks. An agent reading this page alone cannot make a `latestBundle()` call without navigating away.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Moderate; covers "what is" and "how to read," but no troubleshooting/FAQ and no symptom-phrased headings ("how do I decode the bytes array", "MVR feed has no historical data").

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; unambiguous prose, consistent product/entity naming.

audit.summary: This is a concise, well-structured conceptual overview of Chainlink MVR feeds that opens with a strong, liftable definition and cross-links cleanly to its API reference and guides. Its biggest GEO strengths are answer-first framing and clean chunk boundaries; its biggest weaknesses are the near-total absence of machine-readable metadata (no JSON-LD, no canonical, no dates), zero on-page code, and thin concrete specifics. It reads like a solid hub page but leaves retrieval and agent-runnability value on the table — good bones, under-instrumented for generative engines.

recommendations.title: Add a minimal, runnable read example
recommendations.where: "Reading MVR Feed Data" section, after the 3-step list.
recommendations.issue: section describes steps but has "0 fenced block(s)".
recommendations.change: Add one tagged Solidity fence showing the `BundleAggregatorProxy` interface import, a `latestBundle()` call, and decoding the returned `bytes` into the example struct (`netAssetValue`, etc.). Keep it ≤15 lines; link out for full guides.
recommendations.why: gives engines and coding agents a self-contained, liftable code answer instead of forcing a navigation hop that retrieval usually loses.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/how-to phrased subheadings
recommendations.where: new H3s under "Reading MVR Feed Data".
recommendations.issue: no headings match how devs query; "MVR feeds only store the most recent data onchain" is buried in a Note.
recommendations.change: add H3s like "How do I decode the bytes array from latestBundle()?" and "Why is there no historical data in MVR feeds?" with the answer in the first sentence.
recommendations.why: symptom/question-phrased headings win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses even when the answer is present.

recommendations.title: Inject metadata: canonical, dates, JSON-LD
recommendations.issue: canonical MISSING, dateModified absent, 0 JSON-LD blocks.
recommendations.change: emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `dateModified`, a canonical URL, and `inLanguage`; surface a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: freshness and schema raise parse-trust (E-E-A-T) for agents; note the `.md` endpoint may strip head metadata — verify against the HTML page.

recommendations.title: Add concrete specifics
recommendations.issue: vague quantifiers "various data types," "Multiple data points."
recommendations.change: state the concrete supported Solidity types (`uint256`, `int256`, `bool`, `string`, `bytes`), what `bundleDecimals()` returns per field, and any field-count limits. Replace "various" with the actual list.
recommendations.why: quantitative/enumerated specifics are among the highest-lift retrieval signals; qualitative-only prose underperforms.

recommendations.title: Add one authoritative external/canonical link
recommendations.change: link to the Solidity ABI-decoding docs for `abi.decode`, and/or the SmartData concept page, near the decode step.
recommendations.why: inline primary-source links raise credibility and citation rate.

recommendations.title: Lead each section with its canonical fact
recommendations.issue: current opener names the contract but not the one-line "how".
recommendations.change: first sentence should read as a liftable fact, e.g. "Read MVR feeds by calling `latestBundle()` on the `BundleAggregatorProxy`, then `abi.decode` the returned bytes." Name the wrong pattern (treating it like `latestRoundData()`/`AggregatorV3Interface`) explicitly as a Don't.
recommendations.why: defends against engines falling back to the generic single-value Data Feed idiom when the page is skimmed.

antiPatterns: Vague quantifiers: "various data types," "more versatility," "most recent" — replace "various" with an explicit type list.
Undated content: no visible last-updated signal (measured: dateModified absent).
No on-page code despite a "Reading … Data" section that implies a snippet.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is referenced on-page — good; verify this URL is actually listed there so the page is discoverable in the index.
JSON-LD/canonical/date emission is largely a site-template concern; fixing it here benefits all Data Feeds pages.
The `.md` served endpoint appears to drop `<head>` metadata; the CLI should pass raw HTML `<head>` for a full machine-readability read.
